about: Captioned App Store screenshots for Chopstats 1.8.0 (the native iOS design). Rendered by render_store.py; rules and re-render steps in README.md. Coordinates in rings/touches/chips are SOURCE pixels of the 1320x2868 capture; crops are [x0, y0, x1, y1] in the same pixels. headline and sub are lists of explicit lines.

frames.notes: Promise: photo to numbers. facts §2 Photo logging (the AI names dishes, states the assumed portion, estimates kcal/P/C/F). The arrow lands on the meal card of that photo (not on the day total, which would read as the photo's calories). Photo: Unsplash License (photos/CREDITS.md); the card's picture is the app's own thumbnail of the same photo (docs/readme/photos/yogurt-bowl.jpg, the demo file). Numbers: ~388 = 146+212+30 kcal, P26 C40 F14 (EN and ZH, scripts/play_screenshots.py demo-file). Crop = the card's own edges.

frames.notes: Correct with a note (new in 1.8.0; the caption does not say so). facts: Edit meal > Correct with a note sends the note with this meal's description, foods and numbers to the AI the user set up; the answer only fills the form and the card 'Changed from your note — not saved yet' lists the changes; nothing is written until Save (meal_editor_screen.dart). Two slices of ONE state of the editor (yesterday's Chicken curry with rice, demo data): the meal's new total, macro bar and items after the answer, then the card, scrolled. The footer between them names the recipient ('Claude (server)': the capture used a fake own server, never a real key), so it is left out and frame 03 can show Gemini. The answer came from a copy of the QA rig's fake own server (stdlib Python on 127.0.0.1, not in the repo) whose canned answer was reworded like a real model's (portion in the name, a plain reason line). Numbers: 640 -> 510 (curry 380 + rice 260 -> 130), P 33 -> 30.5, C 71 -> 42.5, F 23; rice ~200 g -> ~100 g. EN note typed 'only half the rice'; ZH note typed 米饭只吃了一半 (XCUITest typeText).

frames.notes: Your AI, no Chopstats account. facts §3 (nine providers with your own key, or your own server), §5 (no sign-up or account; key in the iOS Keychain). Settings with Gemini picked (a placeholder key 'demo-key-not-real' was typed so the first-run card is gone, as on a set-up phone; nothing was sent with it). The ring is on the AI Provider row. Both crops end above their footers: Settings' footer says the key is 'stored only on this phone' (not accurate: the Keychain item comes back with a phone backup; owner OK 2026-11-13), and the AI Provider page's footer has 'free tier' / 'charge' (no pricing terms). The API Key provider list is NOT used: it shows 'free tier' / VPN notes. Check rows name no provider (no third-party marks in added text). The large titles show the native iOS design.

frames.notes: My usual foods. facts §2: meals logged on at least 2 of the last 90 days; tap to log again with no photo and no AI; nothing is sent. Every row's kcal/macros equal the demo file's item sums (Mapo tofu with rice 590 = 330+260, P23 C67 F24). Neither language shows 'Around this time' (that header needs a meal logged within 2 h of the capture's clock on 2 of the last 30 days; EN was captured about 22:34, ZH about 21:42), so both lists start with the yogurt bowl logged today at 08:04 (EN in 12-hour form, 'Logged today at 8:04 AM', as on a US iPhone). EN crop ends in the white gap above the Hummus row's divider. The touch point sits on blank row space, not on text.

frames.notes: Privacy, new captions for 1.8.0: iCloud Backup is on by default, so 'Your log stays on your phone' is no longer the whole truth. facts §5: no ads, no analytics/tracking SDK; open source (MIT); the app asks first and names the company; Chopstats has no backend and the developer receives none of your data; iCloud Backup copies the log to the user's own iCloud Drive (API keys never included). Added text says 'your own cloud drive', never iCloud (an Apple mark). The picture is the day log (today's day page: ~1,896 kcal = 388+587+130+791, 4 meals) plus CSS check rows.
